page: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is a shared-core instance within the f1 server family. It is provisioned with 1 virtual CPU mapped to a shared Intel Xeon x86_64 physical core and 0.6 GB of system RAM. The CPU cache layout includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 38 MB L3 cache. Supported ISA extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES encryption acceleration, FMA, and BMI2. This instance lacks dedicated local NVMe or SSD storage and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Synthetic benchmarks reflect the constrained, burstable allocation model of the instance. In stress-ng execution, both single-core and multi-core CPU metrics reach 384.79, placing performance in the lower 10th percentile across tested platforms. PassMark benchmarks show an overall CPU score of 236.08, extended instruction performance of 203.47, and encryption test throughput of 73.1. Large-block write bandwidth measures 0.2 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reaches 0.22 GB/sec and Redis SET performance registers at 0.24 million operations per second.

Given its fractioned CPU allocation and tight 0.6 GB memory threshold, f1-micro offers a minimal cost profile suited for low-overhead entry-level tasks. Resource limitations make it unsuited for memory-intensive applications, heavy database engines, or continuous parallel computation. It is best deployed for lightweight background tasks, simple microservices, basic health-check proxies, or low-traffic administrative utilities where resource consumption is predictable and minimal.
description: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is a shared-core virtual instance designed for lightweight operational tasks. Built on x86_64 Intel Xeon hardware, it provides 1 vCPU with a shared physical core and 0.6 GB of memory. The CPU architecture supports AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA instruction sets. Featuring no attached local storage, the instance exhibits low synthetic benchmark scores across CPU, memory write, and web serving tests, consistently ranking in the lower 10th percentile. Memory write bandwidth registers at 0.2 GB/sec, and static web throughput reaches 0.22 GB/sec. Due to its minimal resource footprint and burstable compute profile, f1-micro provides cost-effective utility for low-traffic services, basic health monitoring, lightweight microservices, and simple background jobs where memory usage remains below 0.6 GB.
